name: Tokyo
utility: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Bureau of Waterworks

supply.note: Tokyo draws principally on the Tone and Ara river systems through the Bureau's treatment plants. No annual production figure with a year attached has been captured.

freshness_note: The water rates have applied since 1 January 2005 and the sewerage rates since 1 June 1998; what changed in December 2019 was the consumption tax multiplier. The ready-reckoner publishing the current totals and the calculation-method page setting out the tables were both captured on 18 August 2026, and the ordinance's amendment history shows no change to the charging articles since Heisei 16.
awaiting: Nothing that holds a figure. A designation of the ordinary residential bore would lift the supply metric from Grade B to Grade A, and the Bureau of Sewerage's own schedule would move the sewerage rate from the collecting utility's table to the levying authority's. Neither changes a number.
open_items: A designation of the ordinary residential bore, which would lift the supply metric from Grade B to Grade A. The ordinance prices twelve and designates none — the same gap as Seoul, and printed as scope rather than treated as a blocker.

The Bureau of Sewerage's own rate schedule for the 23 wards. The rate is now read from the waterworks bureau's own table rather than from a ready-reckoner, which is a real improvement and still one remove from the authority that levies it.
grade_note: Grade B, and not for a missing rate or a missing instrument. Both charging articles are read from the ordinance, the sewerage table from the Bureau's own schedule, and the waiver from the announcement that made it. The reading reconciles against the publisher's own figures at seven volumes, three of them on bills issued under the waiver. It is held below A on the one question a rate table cannot answer: which connection the reference household has.
why_this_city_matters: Tokyo is the Index's clearest demonstration that a published price and a payable price are different objects. A household on a 20 mm connection is charged ¥140.80 per 1,000 litres by the standing tariff and pays ¥55 for four months of the year, because the metropolis waives the basic charge each summer out of general revenue. One figure would have been a lie whichever one was chosen. Both are now reconciled against the Bureau's own bills, which is rarer than it sounds: relief measures are usually announced and almost never illustrated.
resolution_note: Both of this city's blockers are closed. The tier table was closed twice over — by the ready-reckoner it asked for and by the supply ordinance underneath it — and the waiver instrument was closed on 18 August 2026 by the announcement of 15 May 2026 and the Bureau's guidance page. What the second closure bought is not a better sentence about the waiver: it is the payable price, which is the headline here and which is now reconciled against two bills the Bureau prints under the relief.
